paper_title: Enhanced Charge Separation in Ternary Bulk-Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells by Fullerenes

qa_pairs.question: What are the key photovoltaic performance metrics for the ternary organic solar cell based on PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM?
qa_pairs.answer: The ternary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM (1:1.05:0.45) solar cell achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 13.42%, a short-circuit current (JSC) of 27.29 mA/cm², a fill factor (FF) of 70%, and an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.70 V.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhanced Charge Separation in Ternary Bulk-Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells by Fullerenes

qa_pairs.question: How does the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM ternary blend compare to the PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC binary blend?
qa_pairs.answer: The ternary blend exhibits a significantly higher PCE of 13.42% compared to the 10.48% achieved by the binary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC (1:1.5) blend. This improvement is largely driven by an increase in the short-circuit current from 23.05 mA/cm² in the binary cell to 27.29 mA/cm² in the ternary cell.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhanced Charge Separation in Ternary Bulk-Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells by Fullerenes

qa_pairs.question: What effect does adding PC71BM have on the exciton separation yield of the non-fullerene acceptor COi8DFIC?
qa_pairs.answer: The addition of PC71BM increases the exciton separation yield of COi8DFIC from 68% in the binary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC blend to 94% in the ternary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM blend. This is attributed to faster hole transfer kinetics and the formation of an electron transfer cascade.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhanced Charge Separation in Ternary Bulk-Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells by Fullerenes

qa_pairs.question: Describe the electron transfer cascade mechanism facilitated by PC71BM in the PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC system.
qa_pairs.answer: The addition of PC71BM enables an electron transfer cascade in the sequence PTB7-Th → COi8DFIC → PC71BM. This cascade reduces the residence time of carriers at the interfaces and effectively deactivates back-electron transfer (carrier recombination loss) from COi8DFIC to PTB7-Th.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhanced Charge Separation in Ternary Bulk-Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells by Fullerenes

qa_pairs.question: How does the hole transfer rate from COi8DFIC to PTB7-Th change when transitioning from a binary to a ternary system?
qa_pairs.answer: The hole transfer from the non-fullerene acceptor COi8DFIC to the polymer donor PTB7-Th is significantly accelerated in the ternary blend, occurring in 8 ps compared to 21 ps in the binary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC blend.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhanced Charge Separation in Ternary Bulk-Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells by Fullerenes

qa_pairs.question: To what extent is carrier recombination loss reduced in the PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM ternary composite at the 160 ps timescale?
qa_pairs.answer: Carrier recombination loss occurring at approximately 160 ps is reduced by more than 50% in the ternary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM composite compared to the binary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC composite.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhanced Charge Separation in Ternary Bulk-Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells by Fullerenes

qa_pairs.question: Compare the surface roughness of the PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC binary blend with the PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM ternary blend.
qa_pairs.answer: The ternary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM composite features a smoother surface with a root-mean-square (RMS) roughness of 3.19 nm, which is nearly half the roughness of the binary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC composite (6.08 nm).
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhanced Charge Separation in Ternary Bulk-Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells by Fullerenes

qa_pairs.question: In femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, what are the characteristic photoinduced absorption (PIA) bands for PTB7-Th and COi8DFIC singlet excitons?
qa_pairs.answer: The singlet exciton state of PTB7-Th is identified by a short-lived PIA band at wavelengths greater than 1150 nm. In contrast, the singlet exciton state of the non-fullerene acceptor COi8DFIC exhibits a PIA band centered at 1030 nm with a decay lifetime of approximately 65 ps.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhanced Charge Separation in Ternary Bulk-Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells by Fullerenes
